source_used: The Edge Malaysia (Reuters text); Reuters blocked
key_facts: ASML CFO Roger Dassen spoke on a call with reporters after Q3 earnings on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026
He opposes a proposal by US Congress, the Match Act, to limit ASML's sales of DUV lithography equipment to China
He said that if passed after the US midterms it would accelerate China's domestic development of rival technology
He said he was "optimistic that common sense will prevail"
quote_evidence: The chief financial officer of top computer chip equipment manufacturer ASML said on Wednesday the company opposes a proposal by US Congress to limit the company's sales of DUV lithography equipment to China as a bad idea.
He added he was "optimistic that common sense will prevail".
why_it_matters_hint: A leading chip-equipment maker warns US limits could backfire.
title: ASML CFO says proposed US limits on DUV sales to China would be counterproductive
